ApprovalSubmission.title: ApprovalSubmission

ApprovalView.description:
``action`` is the exact payload the digest binds, recomputed before it is shown.

``request.payload.sha256`` is the digest of that action, not of the artifact the ref
names. ``payload_artifact_sha256`` covers the artifact: its download's bytes and ETag.
ApprovalView.title: ApprovalView

CampaignView.description: Authoritative status from the campaign's checkpoint. Safe to read after reconnect.
CampaignView.title: CampaignView

CapsuleInfo.description: A capsule stored as a project artifact. ``artifact.id`` is the capsule id.
CapsuleInfo.title: CapsuleInfo

CapsulePayloadV2.description: Failure Capsule for any registered world. v1 capsules stay valid and replayable.
CapsulePayloadV2.title: CapsulePayloadV2

CapsuleV1.description: On-disk v1 envelope. sha256 is accidental-change detection, not authorship.
CapsuleV1.title: CapsuleV1

CapsuleV2.description:
v2 has no separate loader yet, so the contract itself verifies the checksum.

The checksum detects accidental change; it does not establish authorship.
CapsuleV2.title: CapsuleV2

Coverage.description:
Whether an experiment tested anything. Null only on a checkpoint older than coverage.

``complete: false`` means a run stopped at its tool cap or a fault never fired: a
clean result from it proves nothing, and only the violations it did reach count.
``faults_triggered`` is null on a checkpoint from before it was recorded.
Coverage.title: Coverage

DecisionResult.description:
The recorded decision. ``resumed`` is false if the campaign could not continue yet.

The decision stands either way; ``resume_error`` says why, and the owner can retry
with ``POST /v1/campaigns/{campaign_id}/resume``.
DecisionResult.title: DecisionResult

ErrorInfo.description: Typed error. side_effect records whether a world action may have committed.
ErrorInfo.title: ErrorInfo

ErrorResponse.description: Every non-2xx body. ``reason`` is a stable machine code finer than ``error.code``.
ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse

EventPage.description: Application events by ascending sequence. Not model-token streaming.
EventPage.title: EventPage

ExperimentEvent.description: Ordered application event for status streams; not model-token streaming.
ExperimentEvent.title: ExperimentEvent

ExtTargetRef.description: A registered target id or an inline deterministic script.
ExtTargetRef.title: ExtTargetRef

JobStatus.description:
This server's background execution for a campaign, beside the authoritative record.

``active``: a worker is running it. ``idle``: paused or finished. ``stalled``: the
checkpoint is unfinished but no worker holds it (a crash, restart or worker error);
the owner can continue it with ``resume``.
JobStatus.title: JobStatus

Principal.description: Identity derived from an authenticated session, never from a request body.
Principal.title: Principal

RealityDiffView.description: A diff with its coverage: alone, a truncated run's diff would read as clean.
RealityDiffView.title: RealityDiffView

RecordedRequest.description: What the target attempted, recorded even when the world rejected it.
RecordedRequest.title: RecordedRequest

Ref.description: Typed pointer to evidence; a digest pins content when it is known.
Ref.title: Ref

RepairView.description:
The repair's recorded assessment; world-specific fields are null elsewhere.

Only ``verified`` means the repair held. ``held_by`` is null unless it did: passing
checks on a run that never got there prove nothing.
RepairView.title: RepairView

ReplayResult.description: Recorded-action replay. It never calls a model, so ``model_calls`` is always 0.
ReplayResult.title: ReplayResult

SessionInfo.description: What the session resolved to. Nothing here is client-selected.

TrustedScope.description: Authority the controller grants for one task. Model output never sets this.

WorldInvariantFinding.description: A verifier verdict from world evidence, never model confidence.

WorldRecordedRequest.description: What the target attempted, recorded even when the world rejected it.

WorldScenario.description: A fault schedule for one world. Model-facing (inside proposals): no free dicts.

post.description:
Approve or reject through M06. The approver is the session, never the body.

``approval_id`` must match the path and ``action_digest`` the request, and the
campaign then resumes under its owner. Knowing an id or digest is not authority.
A retry with the same key returns the recorded decision.

post.description:
Start a campaign in the session's project.

The campaign id is derived from the session and the key, so a retry finds the same
campaign and its current state instead of starting another. Reusing a key with a
different spec is a 409. The world, budget and inference gates run before anything
is stored. ``service-relay/1`` is a registered design, not a runnable world: 403.
Text shaped like a credential is refused (422), not stored. ``scripted_scenario``
selects a checked-in proposal on a ``--scripted`` server; anywhere else, or for a world
without that scenario, it is a 422 with reason ``scripted_scenario_unavailable``. A key
reused with another scenario is a 409, as for another spec.

post.description:
Stop a running, paused or stalled campaign at its next guard. Repeating is harmless.

A 202 means it stopped, or a worker has the request: read ``job.cancel_requested`` and
the status. A 409 with reason ``cancel_incomplete`` means the campaign could not be
stopped because its interrupted step can't finish; it is unchanged, and ``job.error``
says why. A finished campaign is a 409 with reason ``campaign_finished``, unless it was
already cancelled. An approval not yet used stays unspent and can't run anything.

post.description:
Owner only. Re-check a paused campaign, or continue a stalled one.

This grants nothing: a pending approval pauses again, and a rejected, expired or
used one ends the campaign. A decision already resumes the campaign, so this is
for retrying after ``settings_changed`` or a stall. A finished campaign is a 409 with
reason ``campaign_finished``, because there is nothing to resume.

post.description:
Validate a capsule, replay it, and store it in the session's project.

An imported capsule is untrusted data. It is identified by its checksum, so a retry
is the same. A capsule that doesn't reproduce is stored and reported as not reproduced.
One that claims what its adapter doesn't do (422 ``capsule_invalid``), or holds text
shaped like a credential (422 ``secret_shaped_text``), is refused and not stored.
